newsitem.title: USA: Reno vows major search for suspected Versace killer.
newsitem.headline: Reno vows major search for suspected Versace killer.

text.p: The FBI is searching intensely for the suspected murderer of fashion designer Gianni Versace and the accused serial killer faces a federal arrest warrant in New Jersey, Attorney General Janet Reno said on Thursday.

"From all evidence that I have, it is a very public, ongoing investigation and the (FBI) is doing everything it can in all its field divisions. We will continue to make sure that we leave no stone unturned," she said of the search for Andrew Cunanan at her weekly news briefing.

Justice Department officials said federal prosecutors in New Jersey late Wednesday filed a criminal complaint charging Cunanan with the May 9 shooting death of William Reese, a caretaker at a national cemetery in Pennsville, N.J.
Justice Department spokesman Bert Brandenburg said the charges carry a maximum penalty of death.
FBI agent Paul Murray said in court documents that Reese's red Chevrolet pick-up truck was missing from the cemetery. It later was found parked near Versace's mansion in Miami Beach, he said.
"A search of the truck revealed, among other things, a Bank of America check bearing the imprinted name of the defendant Cunanan as well as a passport in the defendant's name," Murray said.
Cunanan was charged with "knowingly and wilfully" killing Reese "by shooting him with one gunshot to the head in a wilful, deliberate, malicious and premediated manner."

Cunanan, 27, also faces murder charges in Minnesota in connection with the shooting death of his former lover, architect David Madson. He is wanted for questioning in two other murders in Minneapolis and Illinois.
Reno told reporters she had been kept advised of developments in the high-profile case.

She rejected criticism from some gay groups that the FBI had not been as diligent as it could have been in hunting for Cunanan, who has been described as a male prostitute with ties to the gay community, until Versace's murder.
"I think that the FBI has been pursuing it vigorously," she said.
